detect-hang.prompt: Run hang detection scan now. Read the 'hangDetection' config from this job definition for per-agent thresholds. Scan all VO agent lock files under ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/state/agents/*/lock. For each lock, check if the age exceeds that agent's hangThresholdMinutes (default 60). For hung jobs: walk the process tree, capture py-spy stack traces for Python processes, classify the hang, decide whether to kill (only if age > killThresholdMinutes), log the incident, and file GitHub issues for new patterns. IMPORTANT: After classifying a hang, check the 'perClassification' section for a classification-specific killThresholdMinutes override. If the hang classification matches a key in perClassification, use that killThresholdMinutes instead of the agent-level one. This allows fast-kill for hang types that are unrecoverable (e.g. stale_task_poll, closewait-tcp-hang). CLASSIFICATION RULES: (1) If any bash subprocess in the process tree is running 'az login --use-device-code', 'az devops login', 'az account get-access-token' (which can silently fall back to interactive auth when tokens are expired), or any other interactive auth command (device code flow, browser-based OAuth, MSAL interactive flow), classify as 'interactive-auth-hang' -- these will NEVER complete in a headless context and must be fast-killed. (2) If a bash subprocess is stuck waiting (not running az login), classify as 'hung-bash-subprocess'. (3) TCP CloseWait check: for the Claude process PID recorded in the lock file, run: Get-NetTCPConnection -OwningProcess <pid> -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.State -ne 'CloseWait' } to find non-CloseWait connections. If the process has at least one TCP connection AND all of them are in CloseWait state (i.e. the above command returns nothing), classify as 'closewait-tcp-hang'. This means the remote API has closed all connections but the local process never called close() and is stuck indefinitely -- it will never recover on its own. Apply the closewait-tcp-hang killThresholdMinutes from perClassification. (4) If none of the above match, classify as 'unknown-hang'. Skip any agents listed in 'exclude'. Output a scan summary at the end. IMPORTANT: Your output MUST use ASCII-only characters. Use -- instead of em dashes, -> instead of arrows (right arrow), <- instead of left arrows, ... instead of ellipsis, and straight quotes instead of curly quotes.
detect-hang.description: Scans for hung VO agent jobs, diagnoses via process tree and py-spy, kills if safe, logs incidents

stale_task_poll.reason: Parent agent is polling a completed subagent task and will not recover on its own. Kill after 75 min (hangThreshold + 15 min grace) rather than waiting for the full agent kill threshold.

closewait-tcp-hang.reason: All TCP connections owned by the Claude process are in CloseWait state: the remote API has sent FIN but the local process never called close(). The process is alive but idle and will never recover -- it is waiting for a network response that will never arrive. Kill after 75 min (hangThreshold + 15 min grace).

hung-bash-subprocess.reason: Bash subprocess (running ADO WIQL query via python/az CLI) has exited but the parent bash shell is stuck waiting. This is unrecoverable -- the shell will not exit on its own. Kill at 25 min, which is within the mAuditor agent kill threshold of 30 min.

interactive-auth-hang.reason: Bash subprocess is running an interactive auth command (az login --use-device-code, az devops login, az account get-access-token with expired token, or similar interactive auth flow). These commands require human input and will NEVER complete in a headless agent context. Fast-kill at 5 min -- no grace period needed.

detect-mScrumMaster.prompt: Run hang detection scan targeting ONLY the mScrumMaster agent. Use hangThresholdMinutes=30 and killThresholdMinutes=60 for this scan (override the config defaults). Scan ONLY the lock file at ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/state/agents/mScrumMaster/lock. If age >= 30 minutes: walk the process tree, capture py-spy stack traces for Python processes, classify the hang, decide whether to kill (only if age > 60 min), log the incident, and file GitHub issues for new patterns. IMPORTANT: After classifying the hang, check the 'perClassification' section in the detect-hang job config for a classification-specific killThresholdMinutes override. If the classification matches (e.g. stale_task_poll -> 75 min), use that threshold instead. Output scan summary. IMPORTANT: Your output MUST use ASCII-only characters. Use -- instead of em dashes, -> instead of arrows (right arrow), <- instead of left arrows, ... instead of ellipsis, and straight quotes instead of curly quotes.
detect-mScrumMaster.description: One-off hang detection for mScrumMaster only with 20min hang / 60min kill thresholds

daily-report.prompt: IMPORTANT: Before generating any report, read and follow ALL rules in ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/config/report-rules.md. Generate the daily 5W incident report. (1) Parse audit logs from ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/output/audit/*.jsonl for the past 30 days to extract run durations per agent/job. (2) Collect all hang incidents from ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/output/pHangScout/incidents/ in the last 24 hours. (3) Count Failures (30d): 'Failures' includes jobs with non-zero exit, hangs killed, stale locks cleared, and any pHangScout incident -- not just explicit exit codes. (4) Collect Bug Autopilot (BAP) performance data: read all run-*-summary.json files from the bugAutopilotPerf.logsPath for the last 24 hours (today) and last 7 days (baseline). Merge per_step_aggregate data across runs. Flag outliers (max > outlierMultiplier * avg), threshold breaches (p95 > stepThresholds), trend increases (> trendAlertPercent vs 7-day avg), and slow bugs (> 2x run average). Compute BAP error rate (percentage of bugs with errors). (5) If no meaningful work was done (no incidents in the last 24 hours AND no interesting runtime trends -- no alerts triggered), do NOT generate an HTML report -- just output 'Hang Scout: no incidents or alerts in the last 24 hours.' and exit. Only generate a full report when there are incidents to report or runtime trend alerts were triggered. You MUST use the fixed template at ${REPO_PERSONAL}/virtual-office/templates/pHangScout-daily-report.html. Read the template file, then replace all {{PLACEHOLDER}} values with actual data. Replace {{VO_SUBTITLE}} with: Agent: Hang Scout | Job: daily-report | Start: <PST timestamp when job started> | Complete: <PST timestamp when report is generated>. Replace {{REPORT_PERIOD_START}} with last report timestamp (or '24h ago') and {{REPORT_PERIOD_END}} with current timestamp. Replace {{TOP_RISK_ISSUE_LINK}} with clickable GitHub issue link if exists. Replace {{INCIDENT_5W_BLOCKS}} with per-incident 5W grid blocks (each incident gets its OWN Who/What/When/Where/Why -- NOT a single overall 5W). Replace {{BAP_PERF_SUMMARY}}, {{BAP_ERROR_RATE}}, {{BAP_PERF_NOTE}}, {{BAP_DURATION_TABLE_ROWS}} with BAP data (use BAP not BA as abbreviation everywhere). For RUNTIME_TABLE_ROWS, include an Analysis column (11th column): for jobs with >100% trend spike, link to known pattern or show 'Unknown - needs investigation'. For RECOMMENDATIONS, use severity CSS classes: rec-critical (CRITICAL items, red), rec-warn (TREND ALERT/RUNTIME LIMIT, yellow), rec-ok (resolved/DATA GAP, green), rec (informational, blue default). For Chart.js data, replace {{TREND_LABELS}}, {{TREND_DATASETS}}, {{BAR_LABELS}}, {{BAR_AVG_30D}}, {{BAR_AVG_24H}} with JSON arrays of the computed data. Save to output/pHangScout/daily-report-YYYYMMDD.html and daily-report-latest.html.
daily-report.description: Generates daily 5W incident report with Bug Autopilot (BAP) performance analysis
